list.name: host
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT host FROM obs.pg_digest_stats WHERE $__timeFilter(window_end) ORDER BY host

list.name: cluster
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT cluster FROM obs.pg_digest_stats WHERE $__timeFilter(window_end) AND host IN (${host:singlequote}) ORDER BY cluster

options.content:
**How to use this dashboard** — answer five questions in order; this dashboard keeps the history (ClickHouse) behind the Overview.

1. **Is the server overloaded?** CPU, load, disk stall.
2. **Is it PostgreSQL?** The cluster's CPU against other process families.
3. **Queries or background work?** CPU by backend type: client queries, or autovacuum, checkpointer, I/O workers.
4. **Which query?** The digests with the largest share of the node's CPU or disk reads.
5. **Cause or victim?** Where query time goes: a query that mostly *waits* is a victim — fix the culprit, not the victim.

**Words used here.** *Digest*: one query shape — the SQL with its values replaced by `?`, so `id = 1` and `id = 2` count together. *Run-queue wait*: time a query was ready to run but no CPU was free. *WAL*: PostgreSQL's write-ahead log; a commit waits for it to reach disk. *Backend type*: what a PostgreSQL process does (client connection, autovacuum, checkpointer, I/O worker…). The full evidence for one moment is in `/api/diagnose` → `postgres_report.overload_cause`.
The query shapes that used the most CPU over the chosen time range, with their waits. Fix culprits (large share), not victims (mostly waiting).

panels.title: Top digests

targets.rawSql:
SELECT s.digest_id AS digest, any(t.digest_text) AS text, sum(s.calls) AS callCount,
  sum(s.cpu_ns) / 1e9 / greatest(dateDiff('second', $__fromTime, $__toTime), 1) AS cpuCores,
  100 * sum(s.cpu_ns) / nullIf((SELECT sum(node_cpu_used_ns) FROM obs.host_stats WHERE $__timeFilter(window_end) AND host IN (${host:singlequote})), 0) AS pctNodeCpu,
  sum(s.disk_read_bytes) / greatest(dateDiff('second', $__fromTime, $__toTime), 1) / 1048576 AS readMBs,
  100 * sum(s.runq_ns) / greatest(sum(s.wall_ns), 1) AS cpuWaitPct,
  100 * sum(s.io_wait_ns) / nullIf(sumIf(s.wall_ns, s.io_wait_ns IS NOT NULL), 0) AS diskWaitPct,
  100 * sum(s.wal_wait_ns) / nullIf(sumIf(s.wall_ns, s.wal_wait_ns IS NOT NULL), 0) AS walWaitPct,
  100 * sum(s.shared_blks_hit) / nullIf(sum(s.shared_blks_hit) + sum(s.shared_blks_read), 0) AS hitPct,
  sum(s.temp_blks_written) * 8192 / greatest(dateDiff('second', $__fromTime, $__toTime), 1) / 1048576 AS tempMBs,
  max(s.disk_estimated) AS diskEstimated,
  sum(s.wall_ns) / greatest(sum(s.calls), 1) / 1e6 AS latencyMsAvg,
  max(s.wall_max_ns) / 1e6 AS latencyMsMax
FROM obs.pg_digest_stats AS s
LEFT JOIN (SELECT digest_id, digest_text FROM obs.pg_digest_text FINAL) AS t ON t.digest_id = s.digest_id
WHERE $__timeFilter(s.window_end) AND s.host IN (${host:singlequote}) AND s.cluster IN (${cluster:singlequote})
GROUP BY s.digest_id ORDER BY cpuCores DESC LIMIT 50

panels.description:
What: the heaviest query shapes over the selected time range: cores, share of node CPU, disk, waits, cache hits, temp spill, latency.
Good / bad: one digest with a large pctNodeCpu is a culprit; high cpuWaitPct / diskWaitPct / walWaitPct with low CPU marks a victim.
If bad: hitPct well below 99% = reads miss shared_buffers; tempMBs > 0 = sorts spill to disk (raise work_mem for that query).
Formula: per digest: cpu_ns ÷ range s; ÷ host_stats node CPU × 100; waits ÷ wall of the intervals that measured them; hit = hit ÷ (hit + read).

panels.title: CPU of the top 10 digests (cores)

targets.rawSql:
SELECT toDateTime(intDiv(toUInt32(window_end), greatest($__interval_s, ${flush_s})) * greatest($__interval_s, ${flush_s}), 'UTC') AS time, digest_id AS digest, sum(cpu_ns) / 1e9 / greatest($__interval_s, ${flush_s}) AS cores
FROM obs.pg_digest_stats
WHERE $__timeFilter(window_end) AND host IN (${host:singlequote}) AND cluster IN (${cluster:singlequote})
  AND digest_id IN (SELECT digest_id FROM obs.pg_digest_stats WHERE $__timeFilter(window_end) AND host IN (${host:singlequote}) AND cluster IN (${cluster:singlequote}) GROUP BY digest_id ORDER BY sum(cpu_ns) DESC LIMIT 10)
GROUP BY time, digest ORDER BY time

panels.description:
What: CPU cores used over time by the ten heaviest query shapes.
Good / bad: steady lines are normal; a line that jumps at the incident time is the suspect.
If bad: put that digest_id into the 'digest' variable to see its calls and latency.
Formula: Σ cpu_ns per flush interval ÷ interval seconds.

options.content: PostgreSQL's own processes over time: client backends run queries; autovacuum, checkpointer and I/O workers are background work with their own fixes.

panels.title: CPU by backend type (cores)

targets.rawSql:
SELECT toDateTime(intDiv(toUInt32(window_end), greatest($__interval_s, ${flush_s})) * greatest($__interval_s, ${flush_s}), 'UTC') AS time, backend_type, sum(cpu_ns) / 1e9 / greatest($__interval_s, ${flush_s}) AS cores
FROM obs.pg_backend_stats WHERE $__timeFilter(window_end) AND host IN (${host:singlequote}) AND cluster IN (${cluster:singlequote})
GROUP BY time, backend_type ORDER BY time

panels.description:
What: CPU cores used by each kind of PostgreSQL process over time.
Good / bad: client usually on top; autovacuum or checkpointer rising during the incident points at background work.
If bad: autovacuum: check bloat and cost limits; checkpointer: raise max_wal_size.
Formula: Σ pg_backend_stats.cpu_ns per flush interval ÷ interval seconds.

panels.title: Disk reads by backend type (MB/s)

targets.rawSql:
SELECT toDateTime(intDiv(toUInt32(window_end), greatest($__interval_s, ${flush_s})) * greatest($__interval_s, ${flush_s}), 'UTC') AS time, backend_type, sum(disk_read_bytes) / greatest($__interval_s, ${flush_s}) / 1048576 AS read
FROM obs.pg_backend_stats WHERE $__timeFilter(window_end) AND host IN (${host:singlequote}) AND cluster IN (${cluster:singlequote})
GROUP BY time, backend_type ORDER BY time

panels.description:
What: storage reads of each kind of PostgreSQL process over time.
Good / bad: on PostgreSQL 18+ io_worker carries the reads of queries; a rise matches query reads.
If bad: see 'Estimated disk reads per digest' below to split io_worker reads per query.
Formula: Σ pg_backend_stats.disk_read_bytes per flush interval ÷ interval seconds (NULL when process.include_io is off).

panels.title: Estimated disk reads per digest (PostgreSQL 18+)

targets.rawSql:
SELECT r.digest_id AS digest, r.cluster AS clusterName,
  io.io_bytes * r.sr / nullIf(tot.total, 0) / greatest(dateDiff('second', $__fromTime, $__toTime), 1) / 1048576 AS estReadMBs
FROM (SELECT host, cluster, digest_id, sum(shared_blks_read) AS sr FROM obs.pg_digest_stats
      WHERE $__timeFilter(window_end) AND host IN (${host:singlequote}) AND cluster IN (${cluster:singlequote}) AND disk_estimated = 1 GROUP BY host, cluster, digest_id) AS r
INNER JOIN (SELECT host, cluster, sum(shared_blks_read) AS total FROM obs.pg_digest_stats
            WHERE $__timeFilter(window_end) AND host IN (${host:singlequote}) AND cluster IN (${cluster:singlequote}) AND disk_estimated = 1 GROUP BY host, cluster) AS tot ON tot.host = r.host AND tot.cluster = r.cluster
INNER JOIN (SELECT host, cluster, sum(disk_read_bytes) AS io_bytes FROM obs.pg_backend_stats
            WHERE $__timeFilter(window_end) AND host IN (${host:singlequote}) AND cluster IN (${cluster:singlequote}) AND backend_type = 'io_worker' GROUP BY host, cluster) AS io ON io.host = r.host AND io.cluster = r.cluster
ORDER BY estReadMBs DESC LIMIT 20

panels.description:
What: on PostgreSQL 18+ (reads done by I/O workers), each query's estimated share of the disk reads.
Good / bad: empty on PostgreSQL 16/17 or without postgres.sql — then use readMBs in Top digests.
If bad: treat the top rows like disk culprits: check their plans and indexes.
Formula: io_worker read bytes × digest shared_blks_read ÷ all shared_blks_read, ÷ range seconds.

options.content: Type a digest id in the 'digest' variable to follow one query shape; the slow statements table shows single slow executions and whether they ran or waited.

panels.title: Calls and latency of the selected digest

targets.rawSql:
SELECT toDateTime(intDiv(toUInt32(window_end), greatest($__interval_s, ${flush_s})) * greatest($__interval_s, ${flush_s}), 'UTC') AS time, sum(calls) / greatest($__interval_s, ${flush_s}) AS callsPerSec,
  sum(wall_ns) / greatest(sum(calls), 1) / 1e6 AS latencyMsAvg
FROM obs.pg_digest_stats WHERE $__timeFilter(window_end) AND host IN (${host:singlequote}) AND cluster IN (${cluster:singlequote}) AND digest_id = '${digest}'
GROUP BY time ORDER BY time

panels.description:
What: calls per second and average latency of the digest typed in the 'digest' variable.
Good / bad: latency rising while calls stay flat means the query waits more (see the wait columns in Top digests).
If bad: if calls rose, find the application that sends it.
Formula: Σ calls ÷ interval seconds; Σ wall_ns ÷ Σ calls.

panels.title: Slow statements

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ts, host, cluster, pid, latency_ms, cpu_ms, digest_id, query
FROM obs.pg_slow_queries WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host IN (${host:singlequote}) AND cluster IN (${cluster:singlequote})
ORDER BY latency_ms DESC LIMIT 200

panels.description:
What: the slowest single client statements in the range (one row per slow execution).
Good / bad: many rows of the same digest at the incident time point at it; a slow row with little cpu_ms waited.
If bad: compare cpu_ms with latency_ms: mostly CPU = the query itself is heavy; mostly waiting = a victim.
Formula: pg_slow_queries rows with latency ≥ postgres.slow_query_threshold_ms; query is digest text unless raw samples are allowed.
